items.title: Chris Parker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 5, 2023
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...it sounded like I was talking about art. And so I — it really rang a bell with me as Lester Young might have said...

ctx.x: Absolutely. They’re totally entwined. And I’ve always related the two things together and sometimes I look at a painting and like let’s see for an example like a Wassily Kandinsky painting — I look at it and I say man that’s Elvin Jones to the max. You know that’s like totally how Elvin Jones would paint if he painted. Or I look at a painting — I mean I listen to a drummer like my friend Steve Gadd you know, and say man that is like photorealism you know, that’s like Chuck Close, he’s so perfect and his technique…

I was watching a video that was connected to a recent trio record and I almost had to wind back a little bit because you were using terms — you were talking about the music but it sounded like you were talking about art. And so I — it really rang a bell with me as Lester Young might have said, because I used to work in aesthetic education and we were always trying to find those connections so to hear you say that I just thought was terrific.

Oh great. Yeah I think in that video for my new CD, “Tell Me” the Chris Parker Trio, I talk about Uccello, a Renaissance Italian painter and he sort of, a lot of people think or agree that he kind of invented perspective because he did this painting that’s very realistic but it also has this depth that he accomplishes by there’s a tile floor and there’s lances laying on the floor and there’s a landscape in the background that kind of recedes even further. So yeah.
